instruction: Add page numbers in the header at the top of every page

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding page numbers to the header instead of the footer (variation of the original task). The evaluator checks if headers contain digit characters indicating page numbers. Similar complexity to the original task, just different location.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical: Verification logic uses weak digit detection instead of checking for actual page number fields - would incorrectly pass if header contains any digits (dates, version numbers, etc.)
Critical: Only checks first paragraph of each header (line 30) - would miss page numbers in other paragraphs
Significant: Early return logic (line 29-33) fails entire check if any section header lacks digits - unclear if this matches instruction intent for multi-section documents
Significant: Cannot distinguish between static text containing digits vs. dynamic page number fields - cannot verify that actual page number fields were inserted
Minor: Checks 'every section' not 'every page' - sections can span multiple pages, so verification granularity doesn't match instruction
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Use python-docx to inspect header XML and check for actual PAGE field codes (<w:fldChar fldCharType="begin"/>, <w:instrText>PAGE</w:instrText>) rather than just checking for digit characters
Check all paragraphs in each header, not just the first paragraph
Clarify the multi-section behavior: should all sections have page numbers, or is it sufficient if at least one section has them?
Consider checking for runs with field codes or using doc.part.element to inspect the underlying XML structure for field elements
